def: A sequence consisting of replacement fields, the escape sequences `{{`/`}}`, and other ordinary characters; whether it is a "format string for args" depends on the number of arguments and on how each argument's formatter interprets its *format-spec*. If it is not a format string, passing it via `format_string` is ill-formed at compile time, and passing it via `vformat` throws `format_error`.
A part of a format string of the form `{ arg-id(opt) format-specifier(opt) }`, which is replaced by the formatted result of the corresponding argument.
When all *arg-id*s in a format string (including those nested in a *format-spec*) are omitted, arguments 0, 1, 2, … are used in order; mixing this with manual numbering makes it not a format string.
The format specification syntax the standard library provides for arithmetic, character, string, and pointer types: `[[fill]align][sign][#][0][width][.precision][L][type]`.

A width measured in terminal columns (field width units); with UTF encodings it is estimated from the first code point of each extended grapheme cluster, with East Asian wide characters and several emoji ranges counting as 2 columns.

The debug representation produced by the `?` type: quoted, with tabs, newlines, quotes, backslashes, and non-printable/separator characters and invalid code units written as escapes such as `\t`, `\u{..}`, `\x{..}`.

A formatter specialization that additionally provides a public constexpr member `set_debug_format()`; calling it is equivalent to setting the type to `?`. Range and tuple formatters call it on their elements by default.

A formatter specialization whose `format` member function is declared constexpr; a call to a formatting function can be a constant subexpression only if all formatters it uses are such specializations.

The representation output by floating-point `to_chars` without precision that has the fewest characters and that `from_chars` on the same implementation can read back exactly to the original value; if there are several candidates, the one with the smallest difference from the original value is chosen, with remaining ties resolved by round-to-nearest.

An object passed as the first argument to a parallel algorithm, whose type (`sequenced_policy`, etc.) declares what kind of parallelization/vectorization the algorithm is permitted, and hence the requirements imposed on the element access functions.

The operations invoked by a parallel algorithm during its execution that are provided by the user or determined by the iterator/element types: iterator operations, operations on elements, and user-provided function objects and the operations they require.

A standard library function specified to synchronize with other invocations (other than memory allocation/deallocation and lock-free atomic read-modify-write), such as `mutex::lock`; calling one in user code of an `unseq`/`par_unseq` algorithm is UB.
